domestic.remittances: FY26 closed at a record $41.6bn (up 8.6% YoY from $38.3bn FY25), re-verified this run; Saudi Arabia ($9.78bn) and UAE ($8.81bn) were the top two corridors, with SBP ending pandemic-era incentive schemes as flows normalised at a higher base (https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/pakistan/saudi-arabia-uae-drive-pakistan-remittances-to-record-416bn-1.500602356, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429234/overseas-pakistanis-send-416bn-in-fy26-as-sbp-ends-incentive-schemes). SBP guides FY27 remittances toward a record ~$44bn. July 2026 monthly print not yet released as of this run.
domestic.current_account: FY26 closed with a full-year current account deficit of $139mn (0.03% of GDP, within SBP's guided 0-1% of GDP range), reversing a $1.838bn FY25 surplus -- re-verified this run: three of four quarters ran deficits (Q1 -$737m, Q2 -$624m, Q4 -$425m) offset only by a Q3 surplus of $1.647bn; record remittances could not offset an import-driven trade gap, and FDI fell 34% YoY to $1.637bn from $2.477bn (https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/2016383, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40430638/fy26-ca-posts-usd139m-deficit). July 2026 monthly data not yet released.
